about: Same five-step ladder as reviews.json (see its 'about'). {X} = the name he picks or types; {a}/{plural} = the kind of thing. 'against' marks the other side (the empty square on the card). · 25 Nov 2026 (the owner, after the content check): every way is a phrase the task's own model texts use (the Model and Guided/Sample steps), three alternatives per move, the moves in the models' order, so Basics teaches what the practice shows. · 'example' on a subject: the five sentences finished for its first answer (eg), each starting with its move's first way; Basics shows them on its card (25 Nov 2026, the owner: immediately likeable).
name: Story
how: A story in five sentences, as the model stories do: set the scene, something happens, the tension, the turn, and looking back.

nameAsk.title: Who is it?
nameAsk.aim: Pick a name for your main character.

notebook: Write your story about {X} in five sentences, one per slot. Then check:
ticks: My first sentence sets the scene.
Something exciting happens in the middle.
I used words like suddenly and at that moment.
The ending shows how the character felt.

subjects.label: A mystery
example: It was Matt's first night alone in the house.
While Matt was watching TV, the lights suddenly went out.
No sooner had he found a torch than he heard a knock at the door.
Luckily, it was only his neighbour with a box of candles.
Looking back, Matt could hardly believe how scared he had been.

subjects.label: An adventure
example: It was Lucy's first hike in the mountains.
While Lucy was crossing a river, she suddenly slipped on a rock.
No sooner had she stood up than it started to rain.
Luckily, her friends found a small cave nearby.
Looking back, Lucy could hardly believe it was the best day of the holiday.

subjects.label: A surprise
example: It was Ana's first birthday away from home.
While Ana was walking to school, her phone suddenly started ringing.
No sooner had she answered than she heard her family singing.
Luckily, they had planned a surprise party for her that evening.
Looking back, Ana could hardly believe she had felt so lonely that morning.

subjects.label: A lucky escape
example: It was Pedro's first day at his new job in the zoo.
While Pedro was cleaning a cage, the door suddenly swung open.
No sooner had he turned round than the monkey ran out.
Luckily, it climbed straight into a tree full of bananas.
Looking back, Pedro could hardly believe he had kept his job.
